key_insight: Grow the Harness learns reusable agent control as executable code, so LLMs focus on task reasoning instead of repeating strategy inside every prompt.
engineering_relevance: This approach can cut inference cost and LLM calls dramatically while keeping agents effective across tasks and smaller deployment models.
method: Start from a strategy-free scaffold with fixed model and tool interfaces.
Use function-level execution traces to isolate failures, then repair a bounded code window jointly.
Accept only improvements that pass a held-out success-first gate, accumulating edits into one shared harness.
evidence_signal: Across BrowseComp-Plus and WebArena-Verified with 4B to 120B models, it achieved the best mean success in 5 of 6 settings and reduced LLM calls by 76.0-91.8% versus Tool-Calling.
watch_item: Because the harness evolves through repeated repairs and rollback gating, performance may depend on trace quality, benchmark-specific tooling, and careful regression control.
paper_title: Grow the Harness, Not the Context: From Strategy-Free Scaffolds to Reusable Specialist Agents
